new_types.name: publication_statement
new_types.description: A title-page or copyright-page statement identifying the edition, editor, publisher, printer, place, date or rights; distinct from the title itself.
new_types.evidence: The English and Sanskrit title pages contain editorial and publication credits; the English title-page verso carries a rights statement.

new_types.name: section_colophon
new_types.description: A closing statement identifying the end of a work or major division, distinct from a heading that introduces a division and from a numbered verse.
new_types.evidence: Short standalone lines occur between the end of one numbered verse sequence and the start of another.

definition_edits.name: section
definition_edits.description: A part, chapter or section of the book, extending across pages and holding its contents and any smaller sections. It may begin with a heading or be identified by a closing statement rather than an opening heading.
definition_edits.reason: Major verse sequences appear to end with a closing line before the next sequence begins, as on PDF pages 94, 185 and 250.

questions: On PDF pages 94, 185 and 250, do the standalone lines close major divisions, and are they separate from the adjacent verses?
On PDF pages 44, 51–53 and 68, are the short parenthesized lines between verses independent labels or notes, or do they belong to the adjacent verses?
On PDF pages 11–14, are all entries in the two-column front-matter list table-of-contents entries, or does it also serve as an index?
On PDF pages 323, 325 and 423, are the short, right-aligned lines between verse groups section-ending statements, and should they be distinguished from headings or verses?
On PDF page 525, is the final centered line a separate colophon, or part of the preceding verse?
Does PDF page 530 contain publisher advertisements that should be distinguished from ordinary headings and paragraphs? The small print is not clear enough to establish its purpose.
